Question: Is the character Echo, coming up in the new series, based on a comic book character? What is her story, her powers, and her place in the Daredevil or Kingpin world?
Answer: Yes, Maya Lopez aka Echo is based upon an existing comic book character In fact the Marvel Comics, Echo has much in common with her MCU counterpart. Maya Lopez or Echo is a character from Marvel Comics. Echo is deaf in the Marvel Comics Universe. As she grew up, she honed her natural talent of mimicry. “My name is Maya Lopez. I'm not sure if I'm still that person. The newspapers called me Echo. That's what I feel like. An Echo. This is my story.” -Echo Originally thought to be learning-disabled, once her teachers noticed Maya’s ability to duplicate musical performances, the formers came to realize she was in fact deaf. William Lincoln aka Crazy Horse Maya was a member of the Cheyenne Nation and her father, William Lincoln, was secretly a mob enforcer for the Wilson Fisk. Lincoln began working for the Kingpin when Maya was only nine years old. Eventually Lincoln lived out his usefulness to the kingpin, and the latter had him murdered. Lopez found her dying father and tried to console her but all he could do was leave a bloody handprint on her face. This inspired the face paint that Echo’s wears on her face. Fisk lied about who killed Echo’s father and became her guardian. The Kingpin recognized Lopez’ incredible abilities, and one day hoped to use her talents in his criminal empire. Over the years, Fisk subtly manipulated her into learning fighting skills as well as the performance arts, in which she excelled at both. She remained dedicated to Fisk and saw him as a father figure. Kingpin lied to Maya and told her Daredevil had killed her father (just like in the Hawkeye series, where Clint actually did). This stoked a hatred and desire to see Daredevil dead. Once she discovered the truth, that it was Kingpin himself that murdered her father, Maya turned on him. Now Echo fights against evil and crime, sometimes even with the Avengers. Echo can duplicate any physical action that she sees, ranging from musical performance and ballet to martial arts and weapon usage. She's able to mimic the fighting styles of others much stronger than herself. She's a highly talented pianist, music composer, artist, ballet dancer, boxer, martial artist, and markswoman. She can echo the movements of anyone she sees, including their fighting styles. She possesses the same photographic reflexes ability that Taskmaster has. Lopez aka Echo is deaf in both the MCU series and the comic books. Echo’s abilities in the MCU works similarly to her comic book counterpart. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: What was your review on the Ashoka season finale?
Answer: I was relatively disappointed in the finale Don’t get me wrong I have loved the Ahsoka series and every part of it. I just wish that the final episode, which seems to be the series finale, could’ve explained more and tied alot of the loose ends left at the end. I think the series would’ve been served better if they had included a couple of more episodes before the finale. The finale just left me wanting for more in a lot of ways mostly because of its inability to fully wrap up the storylines that they started satisfactorilyat least. Ahsoka did a wonderul job of introducing fascinating new characters like Baylan Skoll, Shin Hati, the Great Mothers and Captain Enoch but as the series went on their time in front of the camera diminished, and their unfinished story arcs left me completely unsatisfied. The series was action packed, each episode was compelling and interesting, and each episode seemed to be building and culminating to a wonderful finale, but that satisfying finale just never quite happened. In fact, the last two episodes seem to be quite disjointed, and it partly had to do with a lot of the characters going their own separate ways. This series started out, with the characters of Baylan Skoll and Shin Hati, but by the time of the finale, the two of them were hardly seen at all. Their stories were lost in the series’ chaos. Very sad for Ray Stevenson’s last performance to end on such a great character but on a really disappointing finale for him. Skoll was a pivotal character both as another example of a fallen Jedi that became disillusioned with the war and took his own path. But also as agent of change who alluded that he sought power enough to reshape the world and the Universe’s destinies. Perhaps Skoll is looking for the Father? But Baylan was a very complex character that seemed to have some good and some bad in him, but felt like he was serving a greater purpose. I really did think that we would have one final lightsaber battle between him and Ahsoka, but that just never materialized and wasn’t part of the story. I guess Baylan finally found what he was looking for which seemed to be a statue representing the Mortis Gods specifically the Father. So I’m guessing he found his unlimited power. I also was very disappointed because I thought that in the finale, Sabine would’ve faced off against Shin again because their entire story arc seemed to be pointing towards their dual and rematch. None of those came to fruition in the finale. It was honestly very unsatisfying. I am happy that Thrawn and the Great Mothers escaped back to the Star Wars Galaxy and I was elated to hear that they were returning to Dathomir. But Baylan was nowhere to be found and marooning Ahsoka, Sabine and Shin on Peridea seemed like a waste of time, and was very unsatisfying as well. There have been many rumors swirling, and it seems like many of these disparate storylines, including characters from Ahsoka, Book of Boba Fett and Mandalorian etc. will have the final culmination of their storylines in one last movie. While I am excited to see them all in one giant movie, cleaning up all the loose ends from these wonderful, storylines and characters that have been flushed out so beautifully by Filoni would’ve been wonderul and made sense before the Mando Movie. No finale between Ahsoka vs Baylan I think that each series should have its own start and finish. I just don’t think that Ahsoka’s series was complete. I mean the Ahsoka series did do the bare basic, which was to bring back Thrawn to the Star Wars Galaxy. I guess that was the only for sure thing that the series was going to accomplish. I just thought I’d see a lot more character developments, and more interactions between the villains and heroes and each other. Besides not having the climactic finishes between the characters like Sabine Wren versus Shin Hati. We also didn’t really really get a full story of Sabine agreeing again to train with Ahsoka, or like I mentioned above as well no final battle between Skoll and Tano. I did really love the vision of Anakin Skywalker’s Force Ghost, looking upon his Apprentice. I think that scene was one of the most important scenes by finally remembering and bringing Anakin Skywalker back as the centerpiece of the Star Wars universe. It was something that was long overdue. And there are many aspects and many characters about the Ahsoka series that I really did love, but I really felt like the finale fell flat and left me wanting for much more. Shin Hati was left to fend for herself by the end of finale Morgan vs Ahsoka was awesome It was wonderful to finally see live action Edga Bridger but his introduction and purpose on this show seemed muted and lost as well. I did enjoy a lot of the Easter eggs and the many cool details and characters that Filoni included, but it wasn’t enough to save the finale for me. Great Mothers resurrect dead Night Troopers Why did Morai leave Ahsoka or the former just scouting around or because of the Mortis Gods? Filoni and Favreau’s movie was announced during Star Wars Celebration Day and it will be culmination of all of these characters and stories. “We're in the right area code," Filoni told Entertainment Weekly. "We are definitely in the right space. I think it's going to be a clamoring of characters saying, 'how do I get in this picture?' And that's what Jon [Favreau] and I have been figuring out." The movie was first announced at Star Wars Celebration, along with two other live-action features. Filoni’s film will tie together the Disney Plus shows (The Mandalorian, Ahsoka, and The Book of Boba Fett) in a “cinematic event" that will take place after the events of Return Of The Jedi and before The Force Awakens. Source: Mando-movie As I mentioned above, there were a lot of storylines, character arcs and and story arcs which should’ve been finished before the end of the series finale. I am content to wait for the movie, but I think there are a lot of these storylines that I discussed that won’t have enough time in a movie to be fully addressed, and the mistake and not including them in Ahsoka was ill advised. Perfect Ending Even though I have to admit the show had the perfect ending. But in conclusion, the Ahsoka finale was very disappointing and left me very unsatisfied. I hope that clears up any confusion ! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: Where did Luke get the Kyber Crystal for his green lightsaber?
Answer: Luke found the kyber crystal on the Imperial Planet, Christophsis In canon, we have never known how or where Luke obtained the kyber crystal that he used when he built his green lightsaber, until now. In Star Wars issue #34, Luke knew that he needed to create and build a new lightsaber after losing Anakin‘s lightsaber and his hand in his fight with Vader. Luke had found a yellow lightsaber when he was traveling around the Galaxy. He used this yellow lightsaber for a time but the lightsaber and kyber crystal were damaged when he fought Killdroids. Skywalker also wanted a new lightsaber because the yellow kyber crystal lightsaber wasn’t built by him and he didn’t feel a strong connection to it. He knew he needed a new kyber crystal and he had heard there were some on the Imperial planet Christophsis. As I stated above, Christophsis was an Imperial planet, but it wasn’t one that had a large garrison, and was rather far from the center of the galaxy. Skywalker entered the local bar, inquiring about rare gems unaware that all of the inhabitants in the bar were going to sell him out and give him to the Empire. But he was saved by a bounty hunter named Gretta. She knew he was Luke Skywalker and still believed in the Jedi, and she knew that Luke was the best chance to end the evil of the Empire. Dr. Cuata In issue #35, Gretta took Luke to a Dr. Cuata who not only worked on fixing Luke’s damaged Lightsaber, but also gave Luke a blank Kyber crystal. After having a vision of Yoda, the blank crystal turned green. Luke didn’t have an instruction manual on how to exactly build a lightsaber, but he used the Force which showed him the way. He found some parts, bought others and finally constructed the green lightsaber that he would use for the rest of his life. I hope that clears up any confusion!
